<div class="portfolio-page">

<header class="page-hero">
<p class="eyebrow">Public research software</p>
<h1>Research software you can check</h1>
<p>The tools answer different biological questions, but I build them the same way. Each one says what it does, uses data you can download and run yourself, shows how sure it is, and stops where the evidence stops.</p>
</header>

<section class="tools-overview" aria-labelledby="overview-title">
<h2 id="overview-title" class="overview-title">The eight tools</h2>
<p class="overview-lede">Grouped by the question they answer. Each one helps with a decision that comes up early, before you spend time or money on a candidate.</p>

<div class="overview-table-wrap">
<table class="overview-table">
<thead>
<tr>
<th scope="col">Field</th>
<th scope="col">Tool</th>
<th scope="col">The problem</th>
<th scope="col">What it is for</th>
<th scope="col">What it adds</th>
<th scope="col">Key skills applied</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr class="overview-row" style="--row-index: 0" data-field="Target discovery &amp; safety">
<th scope="row" rowspan="3" class="field-cell">Target discovery &amp; safety</th>
<td data-label="Tool"><span class="tool-name">TargetIntel-IO</span></td>
<td data-label="The problem">A gene linked to disease is not automatically a good drug target, yet most tools collapse that judgement into a single score.</td>
<td data-label="What it is for">Sorting candidate genes into genuine targets, biomarkers, resistance mechanisms and poor candidates.</td>
<td data-label="What it adds">Three separate rankings, one per therapeutic strategy, plus the evidence for and against each call.</td>
<td data-label="Key skills applied"><ul class="skill-tags"><li>Open Targets &amp; DepMap</li><li>DuckDB</li><li>Benchmarking</li><li>Sensitivity analysis</li><li>Grounded LLM synthesis</li><li>GraphRAG</li><li>CI/CD</li></ul></td>
</tr>
<tr class="overview-row" style="--row-index: 1" data-field="Target discovery &amp; safety">
<td data-label="Tool"><span class="tool-name">Activation Liability</span></td>
<td data-label="The problem">A target can look safely tumour-specific in healthy resting tissue and stop looking that way once the tissue is inflamed.</td>
<td data-label="What it is for">Spotting targets whose apparent safety margin shrinks under immune activation.</td>
<td data-label="What it adds">A direct resting-versus-activated comparison in public data, with abstention when the evidence is too thin.</td>
<td data-label="Key skills applied"><ul class="skill-tags"><li>Single-cell RNA-seq</li><li>Public GEO cohorts</li><li>Negative-binomial models</li><li>Donor-level robustness</li><li>Reproducible manifests</li></ul></td>
</tr>
<tr class="overview-row" style="--row-index: 2" data-field="Target discovery &amp; safety">
<td data-label="Tool"><span class="tool-name">reach-gap</span></td>
<td data-label="The problem">A target can be highly expressed and still sit too far from a working blood vessel for an antibody to reach it.</td>
<td data-label="What it is for">Asking whether target-positive tumour cells are physically accessible to an antibody.</td>
<td data-label="What it adds">Mechanistic diffusion modelling paired with an evidence graph that returns <code>NOT_COMPUTED</code> rather than guessing.</td>
<td data-label="Key skills applied"><ul class="skill-tags"><li>Reaction–diffusion modelling</li><li>Spatial transcriptomics</li><li>Uncertainty propagation</li><li>Evidence provenance</li><li>Docker</li></ul></td>
</tr>
<tr class="overview-row" style="--row-index: 3" data-field="Method reliability">
<th scope="row" rowspan="2" class="field-cell">Method reliability</th>
<td data-label="Tool"><span class="tool-name">segmentation-fragility</span></td>
<td data-label="The problem">In spatial data, a small change in where a cell boundary is drawn can move a marker between cell types and flip the conclusion.</td>
<td data-label="What it is for">Testing whether a spatial-transcriptomics claim survives a change in transcript-to-cell assignment.</td>
<td data-label="What it adds">Each claim is labelled robust, segmentation-sensitive or not reportable, instead of trusting one segmentation as final.</td>
<td data-label="Key skills applied"><ul class="skill-tags"><li>Xenium / ProSeg / Baysor</li><li>Claim-level auditing</li><li>Planted-truth simulation</li><li>Abstention logic</li></ul></td>
</tr>
<tr class="overview-row" style="--row-index: 4" data-field="Method reliability">
<td data-label="Tool"><span class="tool-name">FM Value Audit</span></td>
<td data-label="The problem">A foundation-model embedding can look biologically structured and still add nothing to a real decision.</td>
<td data-label="What it is for">Testing whether single-cell foundation models beat cheaper baselines at target prioritisation.</td>
<td data-label="What it adds">A leakage-aware temporal holdout designed to report a negative result when that is what the data shows.</td>
<td data-label="Key skills applied"><ul class="skill-tags"><li>Geneformer &amp; scGPT</li><li>Leakage control</li><li>Temporal holdout</li><li>AUPRC benchmarking</li><li>Preregistration</li></ul></td>
</tr>
<tr class="overview-row" style="--row-index: 5" data-field="Drug response prediction">
<th scope="row" class="field-cell">Drug response prediction</th>
<td data-label="Tool"><span class="tool-name">DrugMatch-Confidence</span></td>
<td data-label="The problem">Cancer models respond very differently to the same drug, and predictions rarely say how much to trust them.</td>
<td data-label="What it is for">Predicting how a preclinical cancer model will respond to a given drug.</td>
<td data-label="What it adds">Every prediction carries a calibrated probability, an uncertainty interval and a warning when the input is unfamiliar.</td>
<td data-label="Key skills applied"><ul class="skill-tags"><li>XGBoost</li><li>SHAP</li><li>Conformal prediction</li><li>Probability calibration</li><li>Grouped cross-validation</li><li>DepMap / PRISM / GDSC2</li></ul></td>
</tr>
<tr class="overview-row" style="--row-index: 6" data-field="Protein deep learning">
<th scope="row" class="field-cell">Protein deep learning</th>
<td data-label="Tool"><span class="tool-name">MTF Prediction</span></td>
<td data-label="The problem">Whether a membrane protein carries transcription-factor-like features can change depending on where you draw its boundary.</td>
<td data-label="What it is for">Screening human and mouse membrane-protein domains for those features under different boundary definitions.</td>
<td data-label="What it adds">The same screen repeated across three boundary conditions, so a result that holds under only one is visible as such.</td>
<td data-label="Key skills applied"><ul class="skill-tags"><li>PyTorch</li><li>DeepTFactor</li><li>Captum integrated gradients</li><li>UniProtKB</li></ul></td>
</tr>
<tr class="overview-row" style="--row-index: 7" data-field="Research engineering">
<th scope="row" class="field-cell">Research engineering</th>
<td data-label="Tool"><span class="tool-name">Dev Autopilot</span></td>
<td data-label="The problem">AI coding agents can move fast through a repository and leave no reliable trail of what changed or why.</td>
<td data-label="What it is for">Running AI agents on real code with hard limits on what they may touch.</td>
<td data-label="What it adds">Separate agents implement, audit and review; deterministic gates decide whether work advances, state survives restarts, and a person keeps merge authority.</td>
<td data-label="Key skills applied"><ul class="skill-tags"><li>Agentic AI orchestration</li><li>Pydantic</li><li>SQLite</li><li>Strict typing (mypy)</li><li>State machines</li><li>CI/CD</li></ul></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>

<section class="project-showcase" aria-labelledby="targetintel-title">
<div class="showcase-copy">
<div class="card-topline">
<span class="project-number">01</span>
<span class="status-pill status-preview">v0.6.0 · Research preview</span>
</div>
<h2 id="targetintel-title">TargetIntel-IO</h2>
<p class="project-kicker">Therapeutic-intent-aware target triage</p>
<p>A deterministic platform for interpreting candidate genes in anti-PD-1-resistant melanoma. It avoids one universal score by separating antibody/IO, resistance-biomarker and small-molecule strategies.</p>
<ul class="check-list">
<li>Stable role classification and three intent-specific rankings</li>
<li>Typed, source-linked evidence with mandatory human-review boundaries</li>
<li>Real DepMap Public 26Q1 dependency layer that never silently changes the baseline</li>
<li>Graph-native evidence with a deterministic, GraphRAG-compatible research-preview export</li>
</ul>
<div class="button-row">
<a class="button button-primary" href="projects/targetintel-io.html">Read the case study</a>
<a class="button button-secondary" href="https://github.com/rsolerortuno/TargetIntel-IO">View repository <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a>
</div>
</div>

<p class="proof-label">v0.6.0 release gate</p>
<div class="proof-stat"><strong>825</strong><span>automated tests passed</span></div>
<div class="proof-stat"><strong>56/56</strong><span>productive artefacts byte-identical after the graph layer landed</span></div>

<p class="proof-note">The benchmark tests implementation consistency. It is not an independent clinical validation dataset.</p>

<section class="project-showcase project-showcase-alt" aria-labelledby="activation-title">
<div class="showcase-copy">
<div class="card-topline">
<span class="project-number">02</span>
<span class="status-pill status-preview">v0.5.0 · Research preview</span>
</div>
<h2 id="activation-title">Activation Liability</h2>
<p class="project-kicker">Detecting hidden safety risk in surface targets</p>
<p>A target can look tumour-selective against resting healthy tissue and lose that selectivity once normal cells are inflamed or immune-activated. <code>alia</code> audits how much of that apparent selectivity survives biologically matched activation.</p>
<ul class="check-list">
<li>Paired resting and activated public single-cell cohorts</li>
<li>Donor-level robustness, negative controls and explicit abstention</li>
<li>Frozen manifests and checksums for every executed cohort</li>
</ul>
<div class="button-row">
<a class="button button-primary" href="projects/activation-liability.html">Read the case study</a>
<a class="button button-secondary" href="https://github.com/rsolerortuno/activation-liability">View repository <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a>
</div>
</div>
<aside class="showcase-proof" aria-label="Activation Liability verified release">
<p class="proof-label">Verified release</p>
<div class="proof-stat"><strong>52</strong><span>automated tests · 85.4% non-I/O coverage</span></div>
<div class="proof-stat"><strong>2</strong><span>evidence types: RNA and paired tissue</span></div>
<p class="proof-note">A liability detector with abstention. It does not predict toxicity or establish a therapeutic window.</p>
</aside>
</section>

<section class="project-showcase" aria-labelledby="reachgap-title">
<div class="showcase-copy">
<div class="card-topline">
<span class="project-number">03</span>
<span class="status-pill status-preview">v0.8.0 · Research preview</span>
</div>
<h2 id="reachgap-title">reach-gap</h2>
<p class="project-kicker">Is the target physically reachable?</p>
<p>A tumour target can be strongly expressed and still sit too far from a perfused vessel for an antibody to engage it. <code>reach-gap</code> combines simplified reaction–diffusion modelling with an explicit evidence graph.</p>
<ul class="check-list">
<li>Separates same-tissue measurement from external validation and literature priors</li>
<li>Relative target ranking across six defensible vessel definitions</li>
<li>Returns <code>NOT_COMPUTED</code> instead of inventing an absolute answer</li>
</ul>
<div class="button-row">
<a class="button button-primary" href="projects/reach-gap.html">Read the case study</a>

<div class="proof-stat"><strong>117</strong><span>automated tests</span></div>
<div class="proof-stat"><strong>20,000</strong><span>uncertainty draws per analysis</span></div>

<section class="project-showcase project-showcase-alt" aria-labelledby="segfrag-title">
<div class="showcase-copy">
<div class="card-topline">
<span class="project-number">04</span>
<span class="status-pill status-preview">v0.5.0 · Research preview</span>
</div>
<h2 id="segfrag-title">segmentation-fragility</h2>
<p class="project-kicker">Does the conclusion survive the segmentation?</p>
<p>In spatial transcriptomics a small boundary change can move a marker between cell types and flip a biological claim. This tool makes the claim, not the segmented object, the unit of analysis.</p>
<ul class="check-list">
<li>Compares claims across Xenium, ProSeg and Baysor with fixed biological anchors</li>
<li>Labels each claim robust, segmentation-sensitive or not reportable</li>
<li>Abstains when claim-specific anchor coverage is insufficient</li>
</ul>
<div class="button-row">
<a class="button button-primary" href="projects/segmentation-fragility.html">Read the case study</a>
<a class="button button-secondary" href="https://github.com/rsolerortuno/segmentation-fragility">View repository <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a>
</div>
</div>
<aside class="showcase-proof" aria-label="segmentation-fragility verified release">
<p class="proof-label">Verified release</p>
<div class="proof-stat"><strong>62</strong><span>automated tests · 90.3% line coverage</span></div>
<div class="proof-stat"><strong>77.1M</strong><span>transcript records in the Xenium perturbation</span></div>
<p class="proof-note">Robust and sensitive refer to a predeclared numerical threshold, not to clinical safety.</p>
</aside>
</section>

<section class="project-showcase" aria-labelledby="fmva-title">
<div class="showcase-copy">
<div class="card-topline">
<span class="project-number">05</span>
<span class="status-pill status-alpha">v0.5.0a1 · Pre-release</span>
</div>
<h2 id="fmva-title">FM Value Audit</h2>
<p class="project-kicker">Do foundation models actually add value?</p>
<p>A leakage-aware benchmark testing whether representations from Geneformer and scGPT improve a real target-prioritisation decision over cheaper, easier-to-explain baselines.</p>
<ul class="check-list">
<li>Prespecified decision metric evaluated on unseen future outcomes</li>
<li>Explicit leakage control across feature selection and tuning</li>
<li>Designed to report a negative result when that is what the data shows</li>
</ul>
<div class="button-row">
<a class="button button-primary" href="projects/fm-value-audit.html">Read the case study</a>
<a class="button button-secondary" href="https://github.com/rsolerortuno/FM-Value-Audit">View repository <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a>
</div>
</div>
<aside class="showcase-proof" aria-label="FM Value Audit current finding">
<p class="proof-label">Current finding</p>
<div class="proof-stat proof-stat-wide"><strong>NOT SUPPORTED</strong><span>static Geneformer geometry did not improve AUPRC</span></div>
<div class="proof-stat"><strong>79,542</strong><span>rows in the temporal holdout</span></div>
<p class="proof-note">The contextual-embedding protocol is preregistered but not yet executed. This release is not evidence that foundation models help.</p>
</aside>
</section>

<h2 id="drugmatch-title">DrugMatch-Confidence</h2>
<p class="project-kicker">Interpretable preclinical cancer drug-response prediction</p>
<p>Five real DepMap/PRISM XGBoost bundles produce continuous response, sensitive/resistant classification, calibrated probabilities, conformal intervals, out-of-distribution warnings and SHAP explanations.</p>
<ul class="check-list">
<li>Training-only feature selection and cell-line-grouped splits</li>
<li>Five-fold out-of-fold evaluation with locked GDSC2 validation</li>
<li>Honest release labels: validated, exploratory or insufficient evidence</li>
</ul>

<section class="project-showcase project-showcase-alt" aria-labelledby="autopilot-title">
<div class="showcase-copy">
<div class="card-topline">
<span class="project-number">08</span>
<span class="status-pill status-preview">v0.6.0 · Research preview</span>
</div>
<h2 id="autopilot-title">Dev Autopilot</h2>
<p class="project-kicker">Persistent, auditable development orchestration</p>
<p>Coordinates implementation, adversarial audit and independent review while SQLite records state transitions, retries, findings and decisions across restarts. Version 0.6.0 hardens that loop against a real autonomous milestone rather than a synthetic one.</p>
<ul class="check-list">
<li>Immutable project charter with a dependency-checked milestone DAG</li>
<li>Mechanical scope, test, context and Git-metadata gates, with bounded autocorrection instead of a terminal stop</li>
<li>Review conclusions bound to an exact diff; any later change invalidates them</li>
<li>Stops at <code>READY_FOR_HUMAN_RELEASE</code>; it never commits, pushes, tags or merges product code</li>
</ul>
<div class="button-row">
<a class="button button-primary" href="projects/dev-autopilot.html">Read the case study</a>
<a class="button button-secondary" href="https://github.com/rsolerortuno/dev-autopilot">View repository <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a>
</div>
</div>
<aside class="showcase-proof" aria-label="Dev Autopilot design principle">
<p class="proof-label">Design principle</p>
<blockquote>Agents advise, implement and review. Deterministic gates decide whether work can advance. A person retains scientific and merge authority.</blockquote>
<p class="proof-note">v0.6.0 was validated end to end on a real TargetIntel-IO milestone: implementation, deterministic gates, adversarial audit, independent review, evidence packaging and <code>READY_FOR_HUMAN_RELEASE</code>.</p>
</aside>
</section>
